This Appeal Coming On For Admission, This Day
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
Though matter is passed over and called again, except counsel for respondent no.1, none others appeared.
Since matter is of year 2018, it is taken-up for disposal.
2. Challenging judgment and award dated 15.02.2018 passed by II Addl.
Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Bidar (for short 'tribunal') in MVC no.140/2016, this appeal is filed.
3. Perusal of memorandum of appeal would reveal that appeal is by claimant for enhancement of compensation.

Since finding of tribunal regarding occurrence of accident, involving insured vehicle and claimant sustaining grievous injuries therein as well as liability of insurer to pay compensation are not in dispute.

From above, point for consideration would be :
"Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation?"
5.
It is seen that appellant/claimant is challenging assessment of monthly income, extent of disability as well as award under other heads.
Though claimant stated that he was 24 years of age working as driver and earning `15,000/- per month same is not substantiated by evidence.
In absence, tribunal considered as `8,000/- which is notional income adopted for the purposes of settlement of case before Lok-Adalath for the year 2015.

sentences.text:
Wound Certificate, Disability Certificate, Medical Bills, Lab Reports, X-Ray Reports,
Prescriptions, X-ray Films etc., marked as Exs.P.8 to P.83 corroborated by deposition of Dr.Rajshekher Sedamkar examined as PW.2, would reveal that claimant sustained fracture of tibia and fibula of both legs, callus fracture and fracture of right patella etc.

As per deposition of PW.2,
implants were inserted.

Percentage of disability assessed is as follows :-
NC: 2023:KHC-K:7391 "i) Mobility component:30%, ii) Evaluation of muscle strength:20% combined, iii) Stability component 10%, iv) Extra points 5%.
The percentage of permanent total partial disability is about 35% of same limb."
Above assessment would appear excessive.
7. In fact, PW.2 has assessed whole body disability at 20% and same is considered by tribunal.
Therefore, there would be no scope for enhancement of extent of permanent disability.
Since tribunal has applied correct multiplier of '18', there would be no scope for reduction for enhancement of compensation under 'future loss of income'.
However, since claimant had sustained more than four grievous fractures, award of `20,000/- towards 'pain and suffering' would be grossly inadequate.
Same is enhanced to `75,000/-.
Award of `1,50,000/- towards 'medical expenses' being against medical bills produced is sustained.

For inpatient period of 11 days, award of `4,000/-
towards 'incidental expenses' would be justified.
However, tribunal has not awarded any compensation NC: 2023:KHC-K:7391 towards 'loss of income during laid-up period'.

Since,
fractures take about three months to heal and in instant case claimant has sustained fracture to both legs which would be appropriate to consider period of lay-off as four months.
Therefore, sum of `32,000/- is awarded under said head.

In view of disability sustained and nature of occupation,
PW.2 has opinioned about implants in situ.
Therefore, a sum of `25,000/- is awarded towards 'future medical expenses'.
Taking note of disability, it would be appropriate to award a sum of `50,000/- towards 'loss of amenities'.
Thus, there is enhancement of compensation by `1,62,000/-.
Point for consideration is answered partly in affirmative as above.

Consequently following :
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
Claimant is entitled for additional compensation of `1,62,000/- with interest at 6% per annum from date of petition till deposit.

(ii) Insurer is directed to deposit said compensation within six weeks from NC:
2023:KHC-K:7391 date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
(iii) On deposit enhanced amount is  ordered to be released.
